clue.text: Salvation Army, its new group give pleasure

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of its are made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a faction is a group within a larger body

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army and its new band set out to cheer people up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal, applied only to the word its; 'give' is a link, since the answer is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfaction is the contentment felt when a wish is fulfilled, a kind of pleasure.

clue.text: Wise man on his own for a day

parts.note: solo means alone, unaccompanied
MON is the abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: A sage spends a day in solitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Solomon, the biblical king, is proverbial for his great wisdom.

clue.text: Try this concoction when dry

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of Try this are blended anew

explanation.surface: An invitation to sample a drink when parched.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dry in the sense of parched means needing a drink.

clue.text: Mark giving a true variation to one's name as written

parts.note: a mark or token is a sign

indicators.note: variation means a changed form, so the letters of a true are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone alters a mark when writing their own name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' is the anagram signal working on 'a true'; 'giving' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's handwritten name, used to authenticate a document, is their autograph or signing mark.

clue.text: A retrogressive attitude for a moralist

indicators.note: retrogressive means going backwards, so the word for attitude is read in reverse

parts.note: a pose is a bodily attitude or posture

explanation.surface: A backward-looking outlook suits a moraliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrogressive' signals reversal, but only of the attitude word: the initial A stays forward at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist wrote fables each ending with a moral lesson.

clue.text: Wrong to be holding people in distress

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the legal term encloses the people

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men means people, persons

explanation.surface: It is wrong to keep people in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal; 'to be' links. A tort is a legal term for a civil wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe suffering or anguish.

clue.text: Outstanding model with wealthy bird

parts.note: O/S is the accounting abbreviation for outstanding, unpaid
the Model T was the classic Ford car
rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: An excellent model with a rich bird on her arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise but is O/S, as in an unpaid bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the largest living bird, flightless and native to Africa.

clue.text: An effort to cut down on fuel along the way

definitions.meaning: a road trip done to save petrol, a jokey reading

explanation.surface: A campaign to use less petrol while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cost-cutting campaign is an economy drive, and a journey driven to save petrol is literally one.

clue.text: One's job visiting

definitions.meaning: a vocation or profession someone follows
paying a social call on someone, dropping in

explanation.definitionFit: A vocation is often termed a calling, and someone dropping in on a friend is said to be calling.

clue.text: Exercise done by a prisoner

definitions.meaning: a limbering movement of the body
a term served in jail, slang for a sentence

explanation.surface: A workout taken by an inmate in the prison yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A limbering movement is a stretch, and in British slang a prison sentence is also a stretch, served or done.

clue.text: Property there I'd meant to convert

indicators.note: convert means change into another form, so the letters of there I'd meant are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone explains they meant to convert a building over there.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a hereditament is any property that can be inherited.

clue.text: I seem distraught in North American plant

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the abbreviation
distraught means upset and disordered, so the letters of I seem are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being upset about a plant from North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distraught' turns I SEEM into EMESI, which goes 'in' NA. Despite the surface, the flower comes from South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesia is a genus of bright annual flowering plants grown as bedding.

clue.text: Cabinet maker

parts.note: reads as a carpenter of furniture, but means the politician who chooses the Cabinet of ministers

explanation.definitionFit: The prime minister, the head of government, appoints the ministers who form the Cabinet.

clue.text: Coins, one is in my possession

indicators.note: one word is in another means it sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone holds a single coin and claims it as their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' is the container signal; 'possession' only completes the surface picture of owning coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins are cash, the everyday stuff of payment.

clue.text: Clashing-without an opponent

definitions.meaning: not going together, as colours that jar

explanation.surface: A fighter left without anyone to clash with.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-matched colours are unmatched, and a champion who has no equal is likewise unmatched.

clue.text: Claimed in broadcast to have healing properties

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of Claimed in are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: An advertisement on air says a product can cure ailments.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicinal substance is one with curative effects, used as a remedy.

clue.text: I'd greased parts that were discordant

indicators.note: parts in the sense of separates and redistributes, so the letters of I'd greased are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone oiled the machine parts but they still squeaked out of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun for machine components but is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been discordant is to have been at odds, out of harmony with each other.

clue.text: Arranged a bazaar as the weather is expected to be fine

parts.note: set means arranged, put in order
a fair is a bazaar or market

explanation.surface: A church bazaar is organised because the forecast is for sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer marked set fair forecasts settled, sunny weather.

clue.text: Book production

definitions.meaning: the first book of the Bible

explanation.definitionFit: The opening book of the Old Testament tells of creation, and a genesis is the origin or creation of anything.

clue.text: A second radio, it is worth having

parts.note: a radio is a wireless set

explanation.surface: A second radio is a handy thing to own.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something valuable or useful to possess.

clue.text: Added an alteration at the back of the book

definitions.text: at the back of the book

indicators.note: an alteration is a change, so the letters of Added an are rearranged

explanation.surface: An extra change has been added at the end of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplementary material appended to the end of a publication is given as addenda.

clue.text: Disease mostly caused by small stones?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the disease is dropped

parts.note: shingles is a painful viral disease

explanation.surface: An illness is blamed on pebbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last S from SHINGLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a mass of pebbles, as found on many British beaches.

clue.text: Concentrated in the past perhaps

parts.note: taken as written
the past is one example of a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Something boiled down and condensed in former times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the past as just one example of a tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means strong and highly focused, as concentrated feeling is.

clue.text: Senior church official

definitions.meaning: a lay officer in some churches, such as Presbyterian ones

explanation.surface: A senior figure in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone older is the elder, and a presbyter or lay leader in a congregation is an elder too.

clue.text: About to turn mad, I am going round the bend getting an elementary substance

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: turn here means change round, so the letters of mad are rearranged
going round means the shortened I am encloses another piece

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter, as in a drain

explanation.surface: Someone driven mad and crazed by bending things finds a chemical substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is the anagram signal for mad; 'going round' wraps the contraction around U, from a U-bend. 'elementary' points to a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadmium is a metallic chemical element, a substance made of one kind of atom.

clue.text: Snake by newsman slipped away

parts.note: Elaps is a genus of venomous snakes, a crossword favourite
ED is the usual abbreviation for an editor, a newsman

explanation.surface: A journalist alongside a snake quietly sneaks off.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has elapsed has passed by, gone unnoticed.

clue.text: Figure produced of horse in time

indicators.note: in tells us the horse sits inside the time

parts.note: noon is a time of day
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A figure is produced of a horse in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'Figure' means a geometric shape here, not a number or a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a geometric shape with nine sides.

clue.text: Publicity note on how to undo a safety belt?

definitions.meaning: a statement issued to journalists for publication

definitions.text: how to undo a safety belt?
definitions.meaning: push the buckle button and let go, a jokey instruction

explanation.surface: A notice explaining how to unfasten a seat belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement handed to newspapers is a press release, and you press then release to unbuckle a belt.
